title: The police ball and the 'cribs' repertoire
summary: At the police ball he knew about five numbers, his 'cribs', tunes a band always had in reserve, and one won him $500 against Joe Oliver.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: And, pooling with Joe Oliver, it went to the side. Because the first big job that I played, I played the police ball downtown. And all those policemen knew me, they knew Joe Oliver. They'd kid Joe Oliver on one stand and they'd kid me on the other. And, I had a couple of crips. I knew about, when I played that police ball, I knew about five numbers that I could play. Paddymore was one, and Harmony Rag was two, and one was a soldier song we played. I can't think of it now. But, we had crips that we played. And, no matter what the band played, I couldn't play, I'd let the band play. And then, when I could play. What did you call that, the crips?

What do you mean? I never heard that term. That's numbers that we knew by head. All numbers, musicians used to play in those days. All bands had a crips. And no matter where he went to play, he'd never play that crips until they jammed him. Just like, we'll say Panama. Well that was our crips. See? That number won me five hundred dollars between me and Joe Oliver.
Well you won the contest then.
